## Visa Guide for: Jordan
**Applicable to:** Indian Passport Holders Only
**Last Updated Officially On:** 2026 (Ministry of Interior e-services visa fee schedule; Jordan Pass minimum-stay terms)
**Information Status:** Current as of August 29, 2026

---

## Overview

### Country Information

-   **Country Name:** Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan
-   **Region:** Middle East (Levant)
-   **Capital:** Amman
-   **Official Language:** Arabic
-   **Currency:** Jordanian Dinar (JOD) — one of the more stable, higher-value currencies in the region, long pegged to the US Dollar
-   **Exchange Rate:** 1 JOD = 134 INR (approximate)

> **Important:** Indian passport holders need a visa for Jordan, but — unlike some neighboring countries — India is one of the nationalities eligible for genuine **Visa on Arrival**, making it a comparatively simple Gulf/Levant destination to visit. The standout option for most travelers is the **Jordan Pass**, which waives the visa fee entirely and bundles in entry to Petra and 40+ other attractions, provided you stay at least 3 consecutive nights.

---

## Visa Type 1: Visa on Arrival (Single Entry)

### Overview

The straightforward default route for most Indian tourists — no advance application needed. Available at Queen Alia International Airport (Amman), King Hussein International Airport (Aqaba, where separate exemption rules also apply — see Special Cases), and most land border crossings. **Not** available at the King Hussein/Allenby Bridge crossing from Jerusalem/the West Bank — travelers using that specific crossing must arrange a visa in advance regardless of nationality. Expect longer queues during peak arrival hours (roughly 6 PM-10 PM).

### Cost Structure

| Cost Component | Amount |
| :------------- | :----- |
| Single-Entry Visa Fee | 40 JOD (~5,360 INR / ~USD 56) |
| **Total Cost** | **40 JOD (~5,360 INR)**, payable in JOD, USD, or by major credit card at the airport counter |

### Mandatory Document Requirements (Type 1)

1.  **Passport Details**
    *   **Validity:** At least 6 months remaining beyond your intended stay, with at least 2 blank pages.
2.  **Photograph**
    *   A recent passport-size photo may be requested, though this is often waived at the airport counter itself.
3.  **Travel Proof**
    *   Confirmed return flight and, in practice, evidence of accommodation for your stay.
4.  **Stay Duration:** Commonly cited as up to 30 days for this route — check the exact permitted duration at entry, since a broader ~120-country visa-on-arrival list saw its standard stay extended to 90 days as of January 2026, and it isn't fully clear from official sources whether this specific extension applies uniformly to India's arrangement as well.
5.  **Extensions:** Visit a local police station before your visa expires to request an extension if needed.

---

## Visa Type 2: Jordan Pass (Visa Fee Waiver + Bundled Attraction Entry)

### Overview

Jordan's most recommended option for tourists planning to visit Petra and other major sites. Purchased entirely online **before arrival** — it cannot be bought after you've entered the country — the Jordan Pass waives the standard 40 JOD visa fee outright, provided you stay a minimum of 3 consecutive nights in Jordan (some general guides cite 2 nights; the Jordan Pass's own India-specific guidance states 3 — follow the official jordan-pass.com terms to be safe). Beyond the visa waiver, it bundles prepaid entry to more than 40 attractions, including Petra (whose standalone single-day ticket alone costs 50 JOD/~$70), Jerash, and Wadi Rum.

### Cost Structure

| Cost Component | Amount |
| :------------- | :----- |
| Jordan Wonder Pass (1-day Petra entry) | From 70 JOD (~9,380 INR) |
| Jordan Explorer Pass (2-day Petra entry) | From 75 JOD (~10,050 INR) |
| Jordan Extra Pass (3-day Petra entry) | From 80 JOD (~10,720 INR) |
| **Total Cost** | **70-80 JOD (~9,380-10,720 INR)**, all tiers include the visa fee waiver |

### Mandatory Document Requirements (Type 2)

1.  **Purchase Before Arrival**
    *   Buy online at the official jordan-pass.com site and save the QR code/confirmation to your phone or print it.
2.  **Minimum 3-Night Stay**
    *   Mandatory to qualify for the fee waiver — leave before completing 3 consecutive nights and border control will charge you the full 40 JOD visa fee on departure, negating the pass's main financial benefit.
3.  **Standard Passport & Travel Documents**
    *   Same passport validity and travel proof requirements as Type 1.
4.  **Present at the Visa Counter**
    *   Show your Jordan Pass QR code at the visa counter on arrival, not the general immigration queue, to have the fee waived correctly.

---

## Visa Type 3: E-Visa (Qualifying Residence-Permit Holders), Multi-Entry & Purpose-Specific Visas

### Overview

Beyond the standard VOA and Jordan Pass, Jordan offers a genuinely fast **e-Visa** track — but only to Indian applicants who already hold a valid residence permit from the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, or Oman, or a valid Schengen visa, US visa, or EU member-state residence permit. For those needing more than a single entry, or for business, study, and work purposes, Jordan requires processing through the Embassy of Jordan in India rather than the VOA/e-Visa system.

### Cost Structure

| Cost Component | Amount |
| :------------- | :----- |
| E-Visa (Qualifying Residence-Permit Holders) | From 23 USD (~2,195 INR) — apply via the Ministry of Interior's e-services portal, eservices.moi.gov.jo |
| Double-Entry Visa (3-Month Validity, Embassy) | 60 JOD (~8,040 INR) |
| Multiple-Entry Visa (6-Month Validity, Embassy) | 120 JOD (~16,080 INR) |
| Transit Visa (Single Entry, 15-Day Validity, Max 72-Hour Stay) | Confirm current fee with the Embassy |
| Student Visa | Approx. 140 USD (~13,350 INR) |
| Work Permit (paid by the employer, not the applicant) | Approx. 300 JOD/year for most non-Arab nationals (~40,200 INR); approx. 180 JOD/year for Arab nationals |

### Mandatory Document Requirements (Type 3)

1.  **E-Visa (Qualifying Permit Holders)**
    *   Proof of your valid UAE/Saudi/Qatar/Bahrain/Kuwait/Oman residence permit, or Schengen/US visa/EU residence permit, plus a confirmed return flight ticket.
2.  **Business/Multi-Entry Visa**
    *   Standard passport and photo requirements, plus an invitation letter for business purposes where applicable — processed via the Embassy of Jordan in India.
3.  **Student Visa**
    *   Letter of admission from the Jordanian university/institution.
4.  **Work Visa**
    *   Letter of appointment/employment from the Jordanian employer, who typically handles the work permit fee directly.
5.  **Transit Visa**
    *   Onward travel documentation showing your final destination beyond Jordan.

---

## Special Cases & Exemptions

-   **Aqaba Special Economic Zone (ASEZA) — Free Entry Visa:** A distinctive regional incentive — if you enter Jordan via the Aqaba Special Economic Zone (King Hussein International Airport in Aqaba, the Port of Aqaba, or relevant land borders in the south), your visa fee is **waived entirely**, regardless of the standard 40 JOD charge elsewhere. This applies as long as you also exit through an Aqaba-area border and stay within the permitted window (commonly cited as up to one month); exiting through a different border typically means the standard visa fee applies retroactively. This can make the Jordan Pass less financially compelling if your entire trip is Aqaba-based.
-   **King Hussein/Allenby Bridge Crossing:** No visa on arrival is issued here under any circumstance — if entering Jordan this way (common for travelers coming from Jerusalem/the West Bank), you must have a visa arranged in advance regardless of nationality.
-   **Overstay Fines:** Commonly cited at approximately 3 JOD per day, payable when leaving Jordan — confirm the current rate, as this can be revised.
-   **Exit Tax:** A 10 JOD land-border exit tax applies if leaving by land, unless you both entered and are leaving via Aqaba.
-   **No Mandatory Vaccinations:** Jordan does not impose strict health entry requirements for Indian travelers, though consulting your doctor about general travel vaccinations is still sensible.
-   **Travel Insurance:** Not mandatory for entry, but strongly recommended given the adventure-tourism nature of destinations like Wadi Rum and the Dead Sea.

---

## Arrival Documentation

-   **Visa Sticker/Stamp (VOA):** Issued directly in your passport at the immigration counter — check the entry date and permitted stay before leaving the desk.
-   **Jordan Pass QR Code:** Present at the dedicated visa counter (not the general queue) to have your visa fee waived correctly on arrival.
-   **E-Visa Approval Email:** Print or save the approval for Type 3 applicants, alongside proof of the qualifying residence permit/visa that made you eligible.
-   **Return/Onward Ticket:** Keep accessible, as immigration officers may request it again on arrival.

---

## Comparison Table

| Feature | Visa on Arrival | Jordan Pass | E-Visa / Multi-Entry / Purpose-Specific |
| :-------------------- | :-------------------- | :------------------------- | :---------------------------------- |
| **Total Cost** | 40 JOD (~5,360 INR) | 70-80 JOD (~9,380-10,720 INR), includes visa waiver + attractions | Varies — from ~23 USD (e-Visa) up to 120 JOD (multiple entry) |
| **Stay Duration** | Commonly up to 30 days | Same as VOA, tied to the 3-night minimum for fee waiver | Varies by category — single entry up to double/multiple entry over 3-6 months |
| **Where to Apply** | At the airport/land border on arrival | Online at jordan-pass.com, before arrival only | Ministry of Interior e-services portal, or the Embassy of Jordan in India |
| **Advance Planning** | None | Minimal — buy online before departure | Moderate to significant, depending on category |
| **Best For** | Quick trips, or travelers not visiting Petra | Anyone visiting Petra and staying 3+ nights — the better financial choice for most tourists | Travelers with a qualifying GCC/Schengen/US/EU document, or those needing multiple entries, study, or work purposes |

---

**Disclaimer:** This guide provides general information for Indian passport holders. Always verify current requirements on official government websites (e.g., the Jordanian Ministry of Interior's e-services portal at eservices.moi.gov.jo, the official Jordan Pass site at jordan-pass.com, or the Embassy of Jordan in India) before travel, as visa fees, stay durations, and the Aqaba Special Economic Zone's exact terms can change without prior notice.
